summary: Shinichi Nakazawa is a scholar in religious studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1969 to 1977. He held posts at Chuo University (~1993-2006), Tama Art University (~2006-2011), and Meiji University (~2011).

Shinichi Tsuda works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and earned his Ph.D. at Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Arthur Llewellyn Basham, later teaching at the Eastern Institute and ICPBS.

Shinjiro Kazama is a linguist who studied at Hokkaido University from circa 1984 to 1992. He held posts at Tottori University (~1996-2001) and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies as professor (~2009).

Shinjo Hinonishi (1924-2016) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Shigeru Gorai. He held assistant professor (attested 1980) and professor (attested 2008) posts at Koyasan University.

Shinjo Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and others, as well as under several traditional and foreign teachers, he served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba (1975-1997).

Shinjo Suguro (1925-2004) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served as vice director at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (1980) and as professor at Rissho University (~1969-1996).

Shinjosei Mochizuki (1899-1990) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University (~1920-1924) and held a post at Tezukayama Gakuin University (~1966-1975).

Shinkai Sugawara (1924-2016) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Waseda University (graduated 1951) and Taisho University (doctoral degree 1991). He served as a professor emeritus at Waseda University.

Shinkan Murakami specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies at Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, Ryujo Yamada, Hakuyu Hadano, and Nobuo Kumagai, later serving as professor at Tohoku University (~1970-1996) and at Seiwa Gakuen College (~1996-2003).

Shinko Nakai (1943-2024) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. After studying at Kyoto Prefectural University (~1962-1966), he had a long career at Bukkyo University (~1970-2014), where he served as president and professor emeritus.

Shinkō Mochizuki (1869-1948) studied under Tokuo Jonobe and attended Bukkyo University, Taisho University, and the University of Tokyo. He served as president of Shukyo University (1914-1928) and held multiple leadership and professorial roles at Taisho University between 1926 and 1942.
Shinobu Arai Apple is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey, teacher Mark Csikszentmihalyi, and academic adviser Robert Bickner.
Shinobu Yamaguchi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Nagoya University in 1995. She held a post as professor at Toyo University (attested 2015).

Shinsho Hanayama (1898-1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Toyo University (~1926-1936) and Kokugakuin University (~1936-1944), and taught Buddhism at the University of Tokyo (~1934-1959).

Shintaro Kitano works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under supervisor Kazunobu Matsuda and has held posts as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2005) and part-time lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 2015).
Shinten Sakai was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Shindo Shiraishi. He held a post at Koyasan University (attested 1959).

Shinya Mano works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He held positions as a part-time lecturer at Waseda University (attested 2015-2019) and as a research associate at SOAS University of London (attested 2019).

Shinya Moriyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo and completed his Dr.Phil at the University of Vienna under Eli Franco, later holding a post at Shinshu University (~2011).

Shiro Matsumoto is a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Waseda, Komazawa, and Tokyo universities under Yasuaki Nara and Zuiho Yamaguchi, and served on the faculty at Komazawa University from 1982, becoming professor from 1995 to 2020.

Shiv Nath Sharma was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post at the Research and Archaeological Department in Jammu and Kashmir (attested 1947) and served as a professor at St. Andrew's College, Gorakhpur (attested 1973).
